text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said that a favourable decision from NATO regarding Hungary's membership should be put to a referendum in the first half of 1999.
- The Prime Minister's Office has established contact with the Agricultural Producers' Interest Protection Federation, which has threatened to impose blockades at border crossings.
- A government decree regulating general contract conditions regarding home savings loans will come into effect today.
- Shareholders of tile manufacturer Zalakeramia approved the closed issue of 900,000-1.2 million shares at the firm's Wednesday AGM.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Vice President of the Tax and Finance Office Szabolcs Vamosi-Nagy said that Parliament is expected to accept within ten days a proposal aimed at easing tax and social insurance burdens on farmers.

- A new bill on refugees has been completed, said Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze adding that a restriction under which Hungary need only receive refugees from European countries will have to be lifted.
- A planned visit to Budapest in late March by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind has been cancelled following the announcement of general elections.

- Chances are high that several years of negotiations between Hungary and the EU on the mutual acceptance of veterinary and plant health protection standards will come to an end this week, said Minister of Agriculture Frigyes Nagy.

- The German bank Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau has cut by 50 percent the interest surcharge on loans granted to the Hungarian Development Bank (MFB), as a result of Wednesday negotiations, said MFB deputy managing director Gyozo Kenez.
- The Hungarian Development Bank is seeking to buy a 53 percent stake in the Diosgyori Machine Factory from the two social insurance funds.
- The top management of Polgari Bank, appointed by the Ministry of Finance, has resigned and has been replaced by persons appointed by the new owner Penzintezeti Kozpont.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Young Democrat Tamas Deutsch requested information Wednesday from the heads of authorities conducting the investigation into the Tocsik scandal.

- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. will invite a pre-qualification tender for the sale of 83.15 percent stake of 831 million forint face value in the Szolnok-based oil exploration company Koolajkutato Rt.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The cabinet is expected today to discuss amendments to casual work regulations and also set to decide on a financial framework agreement to be concluded between the Hungarian government and the Helsinki-based Northern Investment Bank.
- Junior governing coalition partner the Free Democrats have begun preparations for the 1998 elections, said party executive Gabor Horn.
- Retail traders and catering companies had combined sales of 191 billion forints in January, 9.9 percent less in real terms than a year earlier.
- The owner South African Breweries of Kobanyai Sorgyar has spent more than HUF 40 billion on modernisation of all production phases of the company since it purchased it in 1993.
- The Hungarian Oil and Gas Co. MOL is preparing to conclude long-term gas purchase contracts with Norwegian firms.
